recipes.title: Banana Oats Smoothie
recipes.ingredients:
1 medium ripe banana (120 g)
40 g rolled oats
200 ml low-fat milk
1 tsp chia seeds (4 g)
3 almonds (5 g)
4 ice cubes
recipes.instructions:
1. Add oats and milk to the blender and rest 2 minutes so the oats soften.
2. Add banana, chia seeds, almonds and ice.
3. Blend 45–60 seconds until completely smooth.
4. Pour into a 300 ml glass and drink immediately.

recipes.title: Mango Yogurt Smoothie
recipes.ingredients:
150 g ripe mango cubes (1 cup)
150 g unsweetened yogurt
50 ml cold water
4 fresh mint leaves
1 tsp flaxseed (3 g)
recipes.instructions:
1. Add mango, yogurt, water, mint and flaxseed to a blender.
2. Blend 40 seconds until creamy.
3. Taste — do not add sugar; mango is sweet enough.
4. Serve in a 300 ml glass, chilled.

recipes.title: Green Detox Smoothie
recipes.ingredients:
30 g spinach (1 packed cup)
80 g cucumber (1/2 small)
100 g green apple (1/2 apple)
15 ml lemon juice (1/2 lemon)
1 tsp soaked chia seeds (4 g)
150 ml coconut water

1. Wash spinach and cucumber. Core the apple; leave the skin on.
2. Blend spinach, cucumber, apple, lemon juice, chia and coconut water until bright green.
3. Serve immediately in a 300 ml glass. Do not store overnight.

recipes.title: Peanut Butter Banana Smoothie
recipes.ingredients:
1 medium ripe banana (120 g), preferably frozen in chunks
1 tbsp natural unsweetened peanut butter (16 g)
200 ml toned milk (or unsweetened almond milk)
1 tsp rolled oats (4 g)
1 pinch cinnamon
4 ice cubes (skip if banana is frozen)
recipes.instructions:
1. Use a ripe spotted banana. For a thicker drink, peel, slice and freeze the banana 2 hours ahead.
2. Add milk and oats to the blender first so the blades move freely.
3. Add banana, peanut butter, cinnamon and ice.
4. Blend 45–60 seconds until completely smooth, with no peanut-butter streaks.
5. Taste — do not add sugar, honey or flavoured peanut butter. The banana is enough.
6. Pour into a 350 ml glass and drink at once. This is a smoothie, not oatmeal in a bowl.

recipes.title: Coconut Water Drinks
recipes.ingredients:
1 tender coconut, or 250 ml fresh coconut water (not coconut milk)
4 mint leaves
1 tsp lemon juice (5 ml)
1 pinch black salt
2–3 ice cubes (optional)
recipes.instructions:
1. Use a tender (elaneer / nariyal pani) coconut — the water should be clear and slightly sweet. Packaged coconut water is fine if it has no added sugar.
2. If using a whole coconut: have it opened, keep the water, and scrape a little soft malai if you like. Do not use thick coconut milk from mature coconut.
3. Pour 250 ml coconut water into a tall glass (or drink from the coconut with a straw).
4. Lightly crush the mint between your fingers, add lemon juice and a pinch of black salt. Stir.
5. Add ice only if the water is not already chilled. Serve immediately.
6. Do not add sugar, honey, soda or fruit syrup. This is a hydration drink, not a green smoothie.

recipes.title: Vegetable Upma
recipes.ingredients:
40 g rava / sooji
1 tsp cold-pressed oil (5 ml)
40 g mixed vegetables, finely chopped (carrot, beans, peas, capsicum)
0.5 tsp mustard seeds
4 curry leaves
1 green chilli, slit
1 tsp chana dal (optional, for crunch)
300 ml water
0.25 tsp salt
2 tbsp coconut chutney (30 g)
4 coriander leaves
recipes.instructions:
1. Dry-roast rava on medium heat 3–4 minutes until it smells nutty; do not brown it. Tip onto a plate.
2. Heat 1 tsp oil in the same pan. Splutter mustard seeds, then add chana dal, curry leaves and green chilli.
3. Add the chopped vegetables and sauté 2–3 minutes until they soften slightly.
4. Pour in 300 ml water and salt. Bring to a rolling boil.
5. Lower the heat. Rain in the roasted rava while stirring so no lumps form.
6. Cover and cook 3 minutes. The grains should be fluffy, not sticky.
7. Rest 2 minutes, fluff with a fork, and garnish with coriander.
8. Serve one 250 g bowl with 2 tbsp coconut chutney on the side. Do not fry a vada with it.
recipes.portionSize: 1 serving · 1 bowl upma (250 g) + 2 tbsp coconut chutney

recipes.title: Oats Upma
recipes.ingredients:
40 g rolled oats (not instant sweet oats)
1 tsp oil (5 ml)
40 g mixed vegetables, chopped (carrot, beans, peas, onion)
0.5 tsp mustard seeds
4 curry leaves
1 green chilli, minced
0.25 tsp turmeric
250 ml water
0.25 tsp salt
2 tbsp coconut chutney (30 g)
1 tsp lemon juice (5 ml)
recipes.instructions:
1. If the oats are large flakes, pulse once so they cook evenly. Do not grind to flour.
2. Heat 1 tsp oil. Splutter mustard seeds, curry leaves and chilli.
3. Add vegetables and sauté 2–3 minutes until they start to soften.
4. Add oats and turmeric. Toast 30–40 seconds so the oats pick up the seasoning.
5. Pour water and salt. Simmer uncovered 6–8 minutes, stirring, until the oats are cooked but not mushy.
6. Finish with lemon juice. The texture should look like savoury upma, not sweet porridge.
7. Serve one 250 g bowl with 2 tbsp coconut chutney. Skip sugar, milk and fruit toppings.

recipes.title: Oats Dosa
recipes.ingredients:
40 g oats flour (blend rolled oats)
1 tbsp rice flour (10 g)
150 ml water
1 tsp oil (5 ml) for both dosas
1 green chilli, minced

0.25 tsp salt

7. Serve 2 crisp oats dosas with 50 g sambar and 1 tbsp coconut chutney — not as a sweet oat pancake.

recipes.title: Moong Dal Chilla
recipes.ingredients:
50 g yellow or green moong dal, soaked 2 hours
40 g onion, tomato and spinach, finely chopped
1 tsp oil (5 ml) for both chillas
0.25 tsp cumin seeds
0.25 tsp salt
2 g ginger
1 green chilli (optional)
30 g mint-coriander chutney (2 tbsp)
1 tsp lemon juice
recipes.instructions:
1. Soak moong dal in water 2 hours. Drain well.
2. Grind dal with ginger, cumin, chilli and salt to a thick, slightly grainy batter. Do not add too much water.
3. Fold in chopped onion, tomato and spinach.
4. Heat a non-stick tawa. Spread half the batter into a 15 cm circle.
5. Cook 2–3 minutes on medium heat with 0.5 tsp oil until the underside is golden and the top looks set.
6. Flip and cook 1–2 minutes. Repeat for the second chilla.
7. Stir the measured lemon juice through the mint-coriander chutney.
8. Serve 2 chillas with 2 tbsp chutney. This is a savoury lentil pancake, not idli.

recipes.title: Egg Bhurji
recipes.ingredients:
2 eggs (100 g)
1 tsp oil (5 ml)
20 g onion, chopped
20 g tomato, chopped
15 g capsicum, chopped
0.25 tsp turmeric
0.25 tsp chilli powder
1 tbsp coriander (3 g)
0.25 tsp salt
60 g whole-wheat flour (for 2 phulkas)
40 ml water for the dough
recipes.instructions:
1. Knead whole-wheat flour and water into a soft dough. Rest 10 minutes, then divide into 2 balls.

5. Pour the eggs into the pan. On medium heat, scramble 2–3 minutes until just set — soft curds, not dry rubber.
6. Finish with coriander. Do not add cream, cheese or extra oil.
7. Serve the bhurji immediately with the 2 phulkas (and cucumber slices if you like). This is a complete plate, not eggs alone.

recipes.title: Vegetable Soup
recipes.ingredients:
40 g carrot, diced
40 g beans, sliced
40 g cabbage, shredded
40 g green peas
20 g onion, chopped
1 tsp oil (5 ml)
2 garlic cloves, minced
5 g ginger, grated
500 ml water or unsalted vegetable stock
0.25 tsp black pepper
0.25 tsp salt
1 tbsp coriander leaves
1 slice whole-wheat bread (30 g)
recipes.instructions:
1. Wash and cut all vegetables to similar small pieces so they cook evenly.
2. Heat 1 tsp oil in a saucepan. Sauté onion, garlic and ginger 1 minute until fragrant — do not brown.
3. Add carrot, beans, cabbage and peas. Sauté 2 minutes so they pick up the ginger-garlic.
4. Pour in 500 ml water or stock, salt and pepper. Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered 12–14 minutes until the vegetables are tender but still hold their shape.
5. For a slightly thicker soup, ladle out one cup, mash or blend it, and stir it back in. Do not add cream, cornflour or soup cubes.
6. Finish with coriander. Toast 1 slice of whole-wheat bread (no butter).
7. Serve 300 ml soup with the toast. This is a clear mixed-vegetable soup, not a salad and not rasam.

recipes.title: Roasted Makhana
recipes.ingredients:
20 g phool makhana / fox nuts (about 2 packed cups popped)
1 tsp oil (5 ml)
1 pinch black salt
1 pinch black pepper
1 pinch chaat masala (optional)
recipes.instructions:
1. Weigh 20 g makhana first — a handful from the packet is usually more than one serving.
2. Heat a wide kadhai or pan on medium. Add the makhana dry and roast 4–5 minutes, stirring, until they feel light and a piece cracks crisply when pressed.
3. Add 1 tsp oil. Toss 2–3 minutes more so every piece is coated and faintly golden. Do not brown them or they turn bitter.
4. Take off the heat. Sprinkle black salt, pepper and optional chaat masala while still hot so the spices stick.
5. Cool 2 minutes. Serve one small bowl. These are puffed lotus seeds, not almonds or popcorn from a packet.

recipes.title: Protein Balls
recipes.ingredients:
4 seedless dates (24 g), soaked 10 minutes if dry
1 tbsp rolled oats (8 g)
1 tbsp natural peanut or almond butter (16 g)
1 tsp flaxseed (3 g)
1 tsp unsweetened cocoa (optional)
1 tsp desiccated coconut to roll (optional)
recipes.instructions:
1. If the dates are dry, soak in warm water 10 minutes, then drain well and pit.
2. Pulse oats in a mixer to a coarse meal (not flour).
3. Add dates, nut butter, flaxseed and cocoa. Pulse until the mix looks like sticky dough and holds when pressed. If it crumbles, add 1 tsp water; if it is too wet, add 1 tsp oats.
4. Divide into 2 equal portions (about 20 g each). Roll firmly between your palms.
5. Optionally roll in desiccated coconut.
6. Chill 20 minutes so they set. Eat 2 balls — not the whole batch. No condensed milk, sugar syrup or ghee ladoo method.

recipes.title: Oats Idli
recipes.ingredients:
80 g oats idli batter (from 40 g dry grain)
30 g onion, finely chopped
30 g tomato, chopped
20 g carrot, grated
1 tsp oil
1/4 tsp mustard seeds
1/4 tsp turmeric
1 green chilli, chopped

recipes.instructions:

4. Serve 3 idlis with the measured sambar and coconut chutney.

recipes.title: Ragi Porridge
recipes.ingredients:
40 g ragi (flakes or groats)
30 g onion, finely chopped
30 g tomato, chopped
20 g carrot, grated
1 tsp oil
1/4 tsp mustard seeds

1 green chilli, chopped

2 tbsp coconut chutney

90 g jowar dosa batter (from 40 g dry grain)
30 g onion, finely chopped
30 g tomato, chopped
20 g carrot, grated
1 tsp oil
1/4 tsp mustard seeds
1/4 tsp turmeric
1 green chilli, chopped
1 katori (120 g) sambar
2 tbsp coconut chutney
recipes.instructions:
1. Spread a ladle of jowar batter thinly on a hot tawa. Drizzle 1/2 tsp oil around the edge.
2. Cook until the underside is crisp and golden, then fold. Make a second dosa the same way.
3. Warm 1 katori sambar and 2 tbsp coconut chutney.
4. Plate 2 dosas with sambar and chutney. Do not add extra oil or potato masala.
5. Eat as a complete breakfast plate.

recipes.title: Jowar Poha

40 g thick poha or jowar flakes
30 g onion, finely chopped
30 g tomato, chopped
20 g carrot, grated
1 tsp oil
1/4 tsp mustard seeds
1/4 tsp turmeric
1 green chilli, chopped
1 katori (120 g) sambar
2 tbsp coconut chutney

recipes.title: Jowar Chilla
recipes.ingredients:
40 g jowar flour
30 g onion, finely chopped
30 g tomato, chopped
20 g carrot, grated
1 tsp oil
1/4 tsp mustard seeds
1/4 tsp turmeric
1 green chilli, chopped
1 katori (120 g) sambar
2 tbsp coconut chutney
recipes.instructions:
1. Mix jowar flour batter with water to a pourable batter. Rest 5 minutes. Add salt, cumin and chopped vegetables.
2. Heat a non-stick tawa, brush 1/2 tsp oil, pour a ladle and spread into a thin round.
3. Cover and cook 2 minutes until the underside is spotted. Flip and cook 1 minute more.
4. Repeat for a second chilla from the same batter.
5. Serve both chillas with the measured mint chutney and sambar as one plate.

recipes.title: Bajra Upma
recipes.ingredients:
40 g bajra rava or broken grain
30 g onion, finely chopped
30 g tomato, chopped
20 g carrot, grated
1 tsp oil
1/4 tsp mustard seeds
1/4 tsp turmeric
1 green chilli, chopped
1 katori (120 g) sambar
2 tbsp coconut chutney
recipes.instructions:
1. Dry-roast the bajra rava or broken grain for 3 minutes; transfer it to a plate.
2. Heat 1 tsp oil. Splutter mustard, then sauté the measured onion, tomato, carrot and chilli for 4 minutes.
3. Add 250 ml water and turmeric; bring to a boil. Stir in the roasted grain slowly so it does not form lumps.
4. Cover and cook on low for 6–8 minutes. Fluff and serve one bowl with the measured coconut chutney.

recipes.title: Bajra Porridge
recipes.ingredients:
40 g bajra (flakes or groats)
30 g onion, finely chopped
30 g tomato, chopped
20 g carrot, grated
1 tsp oil
1/4 tsp mustard seeds
1/4 tsp turmeric
1 green chilli, chopped
1 katori (120 g) sambar
2 tbsp coconut chutney
recipes.instructions:
1. Rinse the bajra. Simmer it with 250 ml water for 12–15 minutes, stirring twice, until soft and creamy.
2. Heat 1 tsp oil in a small pan. Cook the measured onion, tomato and carrot with mustard, turmeric and chilli for 4 minutes.
3. Fold the cooked vegetables through the porridge and simmer 2 minutes.
4. Serve one measured bowl while hot. Keep the sambar and chutney for another meal.

recipes.title: Bajra Idli
recipes.ingredients:
80 g bajra idli batter (from 40 g dry grain)
30 g onion, finely chopped
30 g tomato, chopped
20 g carrot, grated
1 tsp oil
1/4 tsp mustard seeds
1/4 tsp turmeric
1 green chilli, chopped
1 katori (120 g) sambar
2 tbsp coconut chutney
recipes.instructions:
1. Stir the measured onion, tomato, carrot, chilli and turmeric into the bajra idli batter.
2. Lightly brush three idli moulds with the measured oil and divide the batter evenly.
3. Steam for 10–12 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Rest 2 minutes before unmoulding.
4. Serve 3 idlis with the measured sambar and coconut chutney.

recipes.title: Little Millet Upma
recipes.ingredients:

1/4 tsp mustard seeds

1 green chilli, chopped

2 tbsp coconut chutney

recipes.title: Barnyard Millet Chilla
recipes.ingredients:
40 g barnyard millet flour
30 g onion, finely chopped
30 g tomato, chopped

recipes.title: Brown Rice Poha
recipes.ingredients:

1/4 tsp mustard seeds

1 green chilli, chopped

2 tbsp coconut chutney

recipes.title: Brown Rice Chilla
recipes.ingredients:
40 g brown rice flour
30 g onion, finely chopped
30 g tomato, chopped
20 g carrot, grated
1 tsp oil
1/4 tsp mustard seeds
1/4 tsp turmeric
1 green chilli, chopped
1 katori (120 g) sambar
2 tbsp coconut chutney
recipes.instructions:
1. Mix brown rice flour batter with water to a pourable batter. Rest 5 minutes. Add salt, cumin and chopped vegetables.
2. Heat a non-stick tawa, brush 1/2 tsp oil, pour a ladle and spread into a thin round.
3. Cover and cook 2 minutes until the underside is spotted. Flip and cook 1 minute more.
4. Repeat for a second chilla from the same batter.
5. Serve both chillas with the measured mint chutney and sambar as one plate.

recipes.title: Mixed Vegetable Dosa
recipes.ingredients:
90 g dosa batter
80 g chopped mixed vegetable
1 tsp oil
1 katori (120 g) sambar
2 tbsp coconut chutney
recipes.instructions:
1. Heat a non-stick tawa and brush it with 0.5 tsp oil.
2. Pour half the measured batter; spread it thin for dosa or leave it 1 cm thick for uttapam.
3. Scatter half the measured mixed vegetable evenly, cover and cook until the base is golden; flip and cook the filling through.
4. Repeat with the remaining batter and oil. Serve both pieces with the measured sambar and chutney.

recipes.title: Mixed Vegetable Paratha
recipes.ingredients:
80 g whole-wheat flour (for 2 breads)
80 g spiced mixed vegetable filling
1 tsp oil
1 katori (120 g) dal
40 g cucumber salad
recipes.instructions:
1. Combine the whole-wheat flour with 45 ml water and knead for 4 minutes; rest the dough for 10 minutes.
2. Divide into two portions and enclose half the measured spiced mixed vegetable filling in each.
3. Roll gently to 15 cm and cook each bread on a hot tawa with 0.5 tsp oil, about 2 minutes per side.
4. Serve both breads with the measured dal and cucumber salad.

recipes.title: Carrot Chilla
recipes.ingredients:
40 g besan
80 ml water
80 g chopped carrot
1 tsp oil
2 tbsp mint chutney
1 katori (120 g) sambar
recipes.instructions:
1. Mix besan batter with water to a pourable batter. Rest 5 minutes. Add salt, cumin and chopped carrot.
2. Heat a non-stick tawa, brush 1/2 tsp oil, pour a ladle and spread into a thin round.
3. Cover and cook 2 minutes until the underside is spotted. Flip and cook 1 minute more.
4. Repeat for a second chilla from the same batter.
5. Serve both chillas with the measured mint chutney and sambar as one plate.

recipes.title: Corn Chilla
recipes.ingredients:
40 g besan
80 ml water
80 g chopped corn
1 tsp oil
2 tbsp mint chutney
1 katori (120 g) sambar
recipes.instructions:
1. Mix besan batter with water to a pourable batter. Rest 5 minutes. Add salt, cumin and chopped corn.
2. Heat a non-stick tawa, brush 1/2 tsp oil, pour a ladle and spread into a thin round.
3. Cover and cook 2 minutes until the underside is spotted. Flip and cook 1 minute more.
4. Repeat for a second chilla from the same batter.
5. Serve both chillas with the measured mint chutney and sambar as one plate.

recipes.title: Pesarattu with Chutney
recipes.ingredients:
80 g green moong batter (from 40 g dry moong)
5 g ginger
1 green chilli
1 tsp oil
2 tbsp coconut chutney
1 katori (120 g) sambar
recipes.instructions:
1. Spread a ladle of pesarattu batter thinly on a hot tawa. Drizzle 1/2 tsp oil around the edge.
2. Cook until the underside is crisp and golden, then fold. Make a second dosa the same way.
3. Warm 1 katori sambar and 2 tbsp coconut chutney.
4. Plate 2 dosas with sambar and chutney. Do not add extra oil or potato masala.
5. Eat as a complete breakfast plate.

recipes.title: Moong Dal with Brown Rice
recipes.ingredients:
40 g dry moong dal
1 cup cooked brown rice (50 g dry)
1 tsp oil
1/2 tsp cumin seeds
2 g ginger, minced
1 clove garlic, minced
1/4 tsp turmeric
40 g tomato, chopped
40 g cucumber-onion salad
1 tsp lemon juice
recipes.instructions:
1. Rinse moong dal until the water runs clear, then soak 15 minutes and drain.
2. Pressure cook with turmeric, crushed ginger, green chilli and water until soft (3–4 whistles).
3. Heat 1 tsp oil, crackle cumin and garlic, pour over the dal and simmer 3 minutes. Mash lightly.
4. Cook brown rice separately until fluffy. Measure 1 cup cooked grain — do not add extra.
5. Plate 1 katori dal with the grain, cucumber-onion salad and lemon.
6. Eat as one complete plate.

recipes.title: Baingan Bharta with Brown Rice
recipes.ingredients:
150 g eggplant (baingan)
1 cup cooked brown rice (50 g dry)
1 tsp oil
40 g onion, chopped
40 g tomato, chopped
2 g ginger-garlic paste
1/4 tsp turmeric
40 g cucumber salad
1 tsp lemon juice
recipes.instructions:
1. Pierce the eggplant and roast it over a flame or at 220°C for 20–25 minutes until completely soft.
2. Cool, peel and mash the flesh; discard the charred skin.
3. Heat 1 tsp oil, cook cumin, ginger-garlic, onion and tomato until thick, then stir in the mashed eggplant for 5 minutes.
4. Finish with coriander and serve one katori with 1 cup cooked brown rice (50 g dry) and cucumber salad.
5. Do not add extra oil, butter or fried papad.

recipes.title: Beans Poriyal with Brown Rice
recipes.ingredients:
150 g green beans
1 cup cooked brown rice (50 g dry)
1 tsp oil
40 g onion, chopped
40 g tomato, chopped
2 g ginger-garlic paste
1/4 tsp turmeric
40 g cucumber salad
1 tsp lemon juice
recipes.instructions:
1. Wash, trim and cut the green beans into 1 cm pieces.
2. Heat 1 tsp oil, splutter mustard seeds, then add the beans, turmeric and 2 tbsp water.
3. Cover and cook 7–9 minutes until crisp-tender; finish with 1 tsp grated coconut and coriander.
4. Serve one katori with 1 cup cooked brown rice (50 g dry) and cucumber salad. Do not add fried papad.

recipes.title: Phulkas with Bhindi Masala
recipes.ingredients:
2 whole-wheat phulkas (30 g flour each)
150 g okra (bhindi)
1 tsp oil in the sabzi
40 g cucumber-onion salad
1 tsp lemon juice
recipes.instructions:
1. Wash and cut the okra into even pieces so they cook at the same time.
2. Heat 1 tsp oil, add cumin, ginger-garlic and onion; saute until the onion turns pale gold.
3. Stir in tomato, turmeric, chilli powder and salt. Cook until the masala thickens.
4. Add the okra, cover and cook on low until just tender. Finish with coriander.
5. Serve with 2 phulkas and a katori salad. Do not add extra oil or fried papad.
6. This is one complete plate — grain/roti plus sabzi together.

2 whole-wheat phulkas (30 g flour each)
150 g eggplant (baingan)
1 tsp oil in the sabzi
40 g cucumber-onion salad
1 tsp lemon juice
recipes.instructions:

5. Do not add extra oil, butter or fried papad.

2 whole-wheat phulkas (30 g flour each)
150 g capsicum
1 tsp oil in the sabzi
40 g cucumber-onion salad
1 tsp lemon juice
recipes.instructions:
1. Wash and cut the capsicum into even pieces so they cook at the same time.
2. Heat 1 tsp oil, add cumin, ginger-garlic and onion; saute until the onion turns pale gold.
3. Stir in tomato, turmeric, chilli powder and salt. Cook until the masala thickens.
4. Add the capsicum, cover and cook on low until just tender. Finish with coriander.
5. Serve with 2 phulkas and a katori salad. Do not add extra oil or fried papad.
6. This is one complete plate — grain/roti plus sabzi together.

recipes.title: Phulkas with Moong Dal
recipes.ingredients:
2 whole-wheat phulkas (30 g flour each)
40 g moong dal (dry)
1 tsp oil tadka
40 g cucumber-onion salad
1 tsp lemon juice
recipes.instructions:
1. Rinse moong dal until the water runs clear, then soak 15 minutes and drain.
2. Pressure cook with turmeric, crushed ginger, green chilli and water until soft (3–4 whistles).
3. Heat 1 tsp oil, crackle cumin and garlic, pour over the dal and simmer 3 minutes. Mash lightly.
4. Cook phulkas separately until fluffy. Measure 1 cup cooked grain — do not add extra.
5. Plate 1 katori dal with the grain, cucumber-onion salad and lemon.
6. Eat as one complete plate.

recipes.title: Tomato Soup with Toast
recipes.ingredients:
200 g tomato
40 g onion, chopped
1 slice whole-wheat bread (30 g), toasted
1 tsp oil
1/2 tsp minced ginger
1 clove garlic, minced
400 ml water or stock
recipes.instructions:
1. Wash and chop every listed vegetable into small even pieces.
2. Sweat onion, garlic and ginger in 1 tsp oil for 2 minutes without browning.
3. Add the listed vegetables, seasonings and 400 ml water or stock. Simmer 12–15 minutes until soft.
4. Blend partly or fully, then return to the pan. Adjust thickness with water, not cream.
5. Serve 1 bowl with 1 slice toasted whole-wheat bread. Eat as the full meal.

recipes.title: Red Rice Chicken Biryani
recipes.ingredients:
50 g red rice (dry)
120 g chicken
80 g mixed vegetables (carrot, beans, peas)
1 tsp oil
1 tbsp lemon juice
1 tsp ginger-garlic paste
1/2 tsp biryani masala
1/4 tsp turmeric
2 green cardamom
2 cloves
1 small bay leaf
5 g mint leaves
5 g coriander leaves
80 g cucumber-onion salad
recipes.instructions:
1. Rinse red rice and soak 15 minutes. Parboil with whole spices until 70% cooked; drain.
2. Marinate chicken with the measured lemon, ginger-garlic, turmeric and biryani masala for 15 minutes.
3. Heat 1 tsp oil, cook onion until light brown, add the marinated chicken and vegetables, saute 4–6 minutes.
4. Layer the cooked chicken with the parboiled red rice, mint and coriander.
5. Cover tightly and dum-cook 12 minutes on the lowest flame. Rest 5 minutes.
6. Fluff gently and serve 1 measured bowl with the cucumber-onion salad. Do not add ghee.
